Football.title: ‘It’s confidential, isn’t it’ – Erling Haaland makes mystery trip during Man City star’s week off from Norway duty
Football.content:
ERLING HAALAND made a mystery visit to Pep Guardiola’s favoured specialist during his week off.

The Manchester City forward was told by his national team coach Stale Solbakken he was not needed for their friendly against Netherlands on Friday.





He teamed up with the rest of the Norway squad at the weekend and was picked to start against Switzerland on Tuesday.

But during his time out, he made a flying visit to Barcelona to visit Dr Ramon Cugat, who has treated a host of City players during Guardiola’s reign.

Solbakken was asked about the visit in the build up to Tuesday’s game and said: “From the little I’ve spoken with him, everything seems fine, so he’ll give it a try now.

“There must be a reason he went to see a doctor – and it’s confidential, isn’t it?”

Sources close to Haaland insist the forward is fine and the visit to Dr Cugat’s clinic was nothing important.

However City are still in the hunt for two more trophies after lifting the Carabao Cup last week and Guardiola will want his star forward in top shape.

The side trail league leaders Arsenal by nine points, but with a game in hand and a match between the two still to play at the Etihad, the finest of margins could make the difference.

But first they will face Liverpool in the FA Cup quarter finals at the weekend to keep their double hopes alive.

But there is a sense that Haaland will have to find another gear if that is to happen.

After a sensational start to the 2025/26 campaign for both club and country, his form has dipped since Christmas.

He has just five goals in 20 appearances since then – and two of those were penalties.

Football.title: ‘Kid is a joke’ – Max Dowman scores wondergoal after amazing run from inside own half sending Arsenal fans into meltdown
Football.content:
MAX DOWMAN scored a stunning wonder goal for England’s Under-19s and sent Arsenal fans into a meltdown.

But it was not enough to book the Young Lions a spot at this summer’s Under-19 Euros in Wales.





The Arsenal forward scored the second in a 6-0 win over Portugal’s Under-19s and assisted two of the other goals.

Dowman, 16, spun a defender in his own half before carrying the ball to the opponent’s penalty area and finding the bottom corner.

The teenager’s stunning solo run came either side of him setting up Chelsea forward Jesse Derry for a brace, with Ezra Mayers, Shumaira Mheuka and Harry Howell also scoring.

It was not enough, however, to secure Will Antwi’s side a spot at this summer’s U19 Euros.

England’s U19s finished second in their qualifying group behind Serbia, who beat them last week.

Dowman’s goal quickly went viral on social media, though, and sparked a frenzy of praise form the Arsenal fanbase.

The account DJN5_ wrote: “Kid is a joke”.



Adeyemi_AFC added: “He’s in good hands the future is bright…we are lucky to have him.”

BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

Others lavished him with praise saying Dowman is so “direct” and others praised the forward’s “control” .

The OTBAnalysis account said: “He needs more game time with the injury crisis growing by the day.”

Fans could get their wish this weekend when Arsenal take on Southampton in the FA Cup quarter-finals.

The Gunners had 10 players pull out of international duty due to injuries and that may open the door for Dowman to start.

Football.title: Top football club’s president involved in car crash on way to stadium with motor left mangled
Football.content:
FENERBAHCE president Sadettin Saran was involved in a car accident while travelling to the Chobani Stadium on Tuesday.

The incident took place in the district of Kadikoy, Turkish media reports.





He was a passenger in the car and suffered bruises, while the driver sustained minor injuries.

However, both were said to be in good condition following the accident.

The car – a BMW – took serious damage to the front, with the bonnet also impacted.

Meanwhile, the other vehicle was damaged at the bumper.

A statement from Fenerbahce subsequently read: “Our President Sadettin Saran was involved in a traffic accident today while arriving at our club.

“It has been reported that our President, the vehicle driver, and the individuals in the other vehicle involved in the accident are in good general health, with no injuries.

“Our President is currently at our club and continuing with his program as planned.



“We extend our wishes for a speedy recovery to everyone affected by the accident.”

It is understood that Saran was travelling to the stadium for a closed-door meeting with club executives.

He attended the meeting even after being affected by the crash.

Saran was appointed the president of Fenerbahce in September, four years after announcing that he would one day run.

The Turkish side currently sit second in the Super Lig table, four points behind Galatasaray having played a game more.

Football.title: ‘Good timing, admin’ – Chelsea’s awkward post instantly backfires during England’s clash against Japan
Football.content:
CHELSEA were left embarrassed by a mistimed social media post promoting Cole Palmer during England’s clash against Japan.

The Blues tweeted out a picture of the Three Lions star’s shirt just moments after he contributed to them conceding at Wembley.





Palmer, 23, gave the ball away in the middle of the pitch as Thomas Tuchel‘s side toiled for an opener.

Within seconds it was 1-0 to the visitors as Brighton’s Kaoru Mitoma finished off a slick counter.

Palmer had the ball nicked off him by Mitoma, who sprinted forward and sent Ayase Ueda through.

Ueda then found Mitoma free at the back post to score a tap-in past Jordan Pickford and Palmer’s error was ruthlessly punished.



In a presumably scheduled post by Chelsea at 8.10pm, 25 minutes into game and just two after Mitoma’s goal, the club put up a snap of Palmer’s jersey hanging in the changing room.

Showing the No7, Chelsea simply put up a lion and England flag emoji with the photo.

But fans couldn’t get over the timing with one saying: “Probably a bad time to post this.”

Another added: “Good timing admin”.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

A third wrote: “This admin must be having conflicts with Cole Palmer cz what timing is this?”

Palmer got the nod in a rejigged frontline missing Harry Kane through injury.

He started along with Morgan Rogers and Phil Foden in a fluid attack lacking a natural striker.

Anthony Gordon was picked on the left with Bukayo Saka and Noni Madueke out after returning to Arsenal earlier in the week.

Palmer assisted for Ben White‘s goal against Uruguay on Friday having come off the bench in an even more patchwork XI named.



That came from a late corner but England could not hang on for a win.

Football.title: Why is Ben White being booed for England?
Football.content:
Scroll to find out the reason why

BIG BEN Why is Ben White being booed for England?

BEN WHITE has returned to the England squad for the first time since 2022 – but it is not the return he expected.

The Arsenal defender was booed as soon as he stepped foot on the pitch and SunSport can explain why.



Why is Ben White being booed while playing for England?

White has not been part of the England squad since exiting the 2022 World Cup in Qatar early for personal reasons.



He never explained the reasons for his departure and subsequently made himself unavailable for selection for the rest of Gareth Southgate’s time in charge.

This has not gone down well with many of the fans.

What happened at the World Cup 2022?

England announced that Ben White left the World Cup camp and flew home early.

An FA statement confirmed: “Ben White has left England’s training base in Al Wakrah and returned home for personal reasons.



“The Arsenal defender is not expected to return to the squad for the remainder of the tournament.

“We ask that the player’s privacy is respected at this moment in time.”

Football.title: Harry Kane OUT of England vs Japan as Three Lions release statement about star striker after training incident
Football.content:
ENGLAND captain Harry Kane has suffered an injury and will not play against Japan.

The Bayern Munich forward was not included by Thomas Tuchel for Tuesday’s final friendly of the season before the World Cup.





A statement from the Three Lions confirmed: “Harry Kane is rested tonight as a precaution having picked up a minor issue in training, but remains with the squad receiving further assessment.”

SunSport understands it is a foot injury that has been bothering Kane in the build-up.

Kane, 32, was one of the many not used for Friday’s clash with Uruguay, also at Wembley.

A set of Thomas Tuchel‘s favourites were granted more time off before the camp.

Kane sat that one out as Tuchel rotated his squad with a view to looking at outsiders ahead of this summer’s tournament.

England could only manage a drab 1-1 draw after conceding a late penalty.

A host of stars have since withdrawn from the Japan match, which will be the last time Tuchel has a camp before naming his preliminary World Cup squad later this year.

He named a huge 35 players for the two matches only for Arsenal trio Noni Madueke, Declan Rice, and Bukayo Saka to head home early.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

They were joined by Manchester City’s John Stones and Crystal Palace midfielder Adam Wharton.

Aaron Ramsdale, Dominic Calvert-Lewin, and Fikayo Tomori were all cut rather than withdrawing.

Although the extent of Kane’s issue has been downplayed, some will no doubt be fearful for the country’s all-time top scorer.

His fitness by the time major international competitions come round has been a problem in the past.

Kane has bagged a ridiculous 48 goals for Bayern already this season in 40 appearances, including 31 from 26 Bundesliga matches.



He missed a 4-1 win over Borussia Monchengladbach earlier in March with a calf strain.

England lined up without a natural striker in Kane’s absence despite Dominic Solanke being on the bench.

Solanke got the nod against Uruguay but was replaced by Calvert-Lewin before the hour mark.

Kane’s usual understudy in recent years, Ollie Watkins, did not get the callup with Marcus Rashford also put in as a sub here.

Football.title: Italy stunned by state of cramped dressing room at Bosnia stadium for World Cup play-off with bucket instead of ice bath
Football.content:
ITALY players were not treated to luxury on their arrival in Bosnia for Tuesday’s crucial World Cup play-off.

Gennaro Gattuso’s stars will have been shocked to enter their tiny changing room for the huge clash in Zenica.





Videos from Italian outlet La Stampa show behind-the-scenes footage of what greeted the Azzurri at the Bilino Polje Stadium.

Upon entering, a small, tiled toilet can be seen on the left before ripped lino flooring leads into the main dressing room area.

A rickety old table is at one end of the room in front of small wooden seating benches for the players.

In the centre of the teeny room is a massage table that barely looks fit to hold half of giant goalkeeper Gianluigi Donnarumma.

A banner above the seats says “Forza Azzurri” with a tattered tactics board held up on the wall as well.

The showers are closer to bleak leisure centre facilities than these footballing aces are used to.

Blue and white curtains hang above the white floor with small nozzle heads.



Instead of an ice bath – now a regular feature at most big European clubs – there is simply a bucket in front of the radiator, jammed in at the end.

SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

The narrow showers wrap up what will certainly be an uncomfortable welcome.

With the ground only holding 15,000 fans, it will have the feeling of an early round cup tie for many.

For the match, which decides who gets into this summer’s World Cup in USA, Canada, and Mexico, only 9,000 will be allowed in due to issues in November’s match with Romania.

And some football supporters aren’t sure this stadium is fit for purpose.



One wrote on X: “If I were them, I’d refuse to play… better they win it by default at the table than set foot in there!”

Another added: “This locker room is embarrassing; at a professional level, locker rooms like this—so ugly and cramped—don’t exist.”

But others were more on board with creating an unsettling environment.

Someone else said: “They do what they can with what they have. Just like it was with us decades ago, when soccer was a sport and a passion, not a sleazy business with money at the centre of everything.”

Italy got through to the final play-off after overcoming Northern Ireland in Bergamo last week.



They once more failed to qualify for the World Cup directly but have an extra chance to do so here after goals from Sandro Tonali and Moise Keane.

Bosnia beat Wales on penalties following a tense period of extra time in Cardiff.

Edin Dzeko scored a dramatic equaliser to force the game beyond 90 minutes.

Football.title: Blackburn boss sparks outrage with controversial Northern Ireland selection for dead rubber against Wales
Football.content:
BLACKBURN manager Michael O’Neill has come under fire yet again after picking players from relegation rivals amid his dual role that also sees him coach Northern Ireland.

O’Neill, 56, saw his 2026 World Cup hopes come to an end on Thursday after the Northern Irish national team lost 2-0 to Italy in their play-off semi-final.



The Green and White Army are playing Wales in an international friendly.



And he has picked FOUR players who ply their trade with Blackburn’s Championship relegation rivals.

Three of them – Isaac Price (West Brom), Jamie Donley (Oxford) and Terry Devlin (Portsmouth) – also started NI’s World Cup play-off vs Italy on Thursday.

Ciaran Brown is the other player starting – before he puts on his Oxford shirt this weekend.

The only Blackburn player O’Neill picked in his squad has started neither game.

And his selection has raised eyebrows with fans on social media.

One wrote: “Absolutely nothing to see here, just two Oxford players and an Albion player starting while the Blackburn player is rested.”

One Oxford fan added: Of course you’re starting our main players in a match with nothing to play for.”

CASINO SPECIAL – BEST CASINO BONUSES FROM £10 DEPOSITS

While another simply wrote that the decision “stinks”.



The Northern Irish tactician has been juggling his role as the national team’s manager since February when he also took over at Blackburn.

Rovers let the experienced head coach remain in international football amid their determination to avoid relegation to League One as they are currently only four points above the drop zone.

According to the Press Association, however, a number of Championship clubs have raised concerns after his most recent call-ups.

The teams contacted the EFL citing a possible conflict of interest as O’Neill could select players who are also involved in the same relegation scrap as Blackburn.

BBC Radio Oxford reported that Oxford, who are second to last in the Championship table with one point separating them from safety, are among those to raise the matter.



The U’s have four players – Donley, Brown, Jamie McDonnell and Brodie Spencer – in O’Neill’s 22-man squad.

Portsmouth – one point above the relegation zone – and West Brom – four points away from the drop – have a player each called up for Northern Ireland in Devlin and Price respectively.

Uncapped teenager Tom Atcheson is the sole Blackburn ace in O’Neill’s squad during the international break.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

The EFL has indicated that international selection is a matter for Fifa and not within their jurisdiction.

Leicester are also embroiled in the Championship’s heated relegation scrap with struggling Sheffield Wednesday already facing up to League One football next season.

Football.title: Tottenham Supporters' Trust issue damning statement after Roberto De Zerbi appointment
Football.content:
Tottenham Supporters' Trust issue damning statement after Roberto De Zerbi appointment

Tottenham Hotspur Supporters' Trust have issued a statement following the appointment of Roberto De Zerbi as head coach, expressing serious concerns over his past comments about Mason Greenwood

View 2 Images Tottenham Hotspur appointing Roberto De Zerbi is not receiving universal approval from Spurs fans (Image: Franco Arland, Getty Images)

The Tottenham Hotspur Supporters' Trust claims that the club's decision to appoint Roberto De Zerbi as their new head coach raises serious, far-reaching concerns. They highlight comments the former Marseille coach made last year about Mason Greenwood, who the French club signed from Manchester United weeks after appointing De Zerbi.

‌



In October 2022, Greenwood was charged with assault occasioning actual bodily harm, attempted rape and controlling and coercive behaviour. However, the Crown Prosecution Service dropped the charges in February 2023.

‌



They did so owing to "a combination of the withdrawal of key witnesses and new material that came to light". The CPS said that meant there was "no realistic prospect of conviction".

‌



The Trust responded to Spurs' announcement of the appointment by releasing its own statement shortly afterwards. It began: "We note the Club's announcement of the appointment of Roberto De Zerbi to the Manager role.

"While we recognise the limited pool of managers with recent Premier League experience, and the need to act with urgency as Spurs face the prospect of relegation, this appointment raises serious and far-reaching concerns, and many fans have been in touch with us to urge us to communicate the strength of feeling. We raised these concerns directly with the Club prior to its announcement.

Roberto De Zerbi makes first Tottenham move by holding talks with World Cup winner READ MORE :

Roberto De Zerbi reveals Tottenham 'ambition' as club make demands clear to new boss READ MORE :

"The Club has previously committed to challenging instances of violence against women and girls and acting with integrity and upholding its values when faced with any incidents. De Zerbi's comments about Mason Greenwood were unnecessary, ill-judged, and deeply offensive to a significant number of supporters."

‌



In November, De Zerbi called Greenwood a "good guy" who paid a "heavy price". The then-Marseille coach said: "It saddens me what happened in his life, because I know a totally different person than the one who was described."

Spurs are understood to have thoroughly examined and discussed the remarks and feelings surrounding Greenwood with De Zerbi during negotiations. Proud Lilywhites, Spurs Reach and Women of the Lane are three supporter groups who voiced concerns before the appointment.

THST's statement continues: "We believe these statements, left unchecked, will create a divide among supporters at a time when we all need to be pulling together to back the team. It is concerning that the Club would put us in this position right when the team needs fans the most.

‌



View 2 Images Roberto De Zerbi coached Mason Greenwood at Marseille (Image: Jean Catuffe, Getty Images)

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

"Fans are rallying behind the 'All Together, Always' initiative, and this appointment places heavy strain on that unity. If those remarks reflect his genuine views, they cast a troubling shadow over the values of the Club we love.

‌



"The Club must reassert its commitment to the values that fans hold dear-chief among them equality, respect, and integrity. With this appointment, communications from the Club and from Mr De Zerbi must clearly and unequivocally reaffirm these values.

"Our preference would have been for a short-term appointment of an individual or individuals who understand the Club and can lead the players in the seven battles to come. There would then have been an opportunity in the summer to attract a wide range of potential applicants with a track record of success in inspiring fans and players: candidates who could lead and develop sustained success for the team, for seasons to come.

"The Club has chosen otherwise. We will continue to support efforts to get behind the team and play our part in preserving the Club's Premier League status, but it is understandable that many fans will do so with a heavy heart.

Article continues below

"Our Five Principles for Spurs ownership include Leading with Integrity and Championing Ethical Standards. At present, supporters rate performance in this area at just 2.2 out of 10. This decision risks further eroding confidence unless addressed with clarity, humility, and decisive action.

"We fully understand that the immediate priority is to avoid relegation. However, this situation is the result of prolonged strategic failings. THST have warned for years that the Club was heading in this direction, and the lack of timely, sound decision-making has now left options severely compromised.

"It will take significant effort for many fans to restore their faith in the Club's leadership. That process must begin with transparency, accountability and a renewed commitment to the principles that define Tottenham Hotspur."

Football.title: Turkey coach collapses midway through game as statement released after medical attention
Football.content:
Turkey coach collapses midway through game as statement released after medical attention

Turkey U21 manager Egemen Korkmaz was taken to hospital after collapsing to the floor midway through his side's clash with Croatia with the coach losing consciousness

View 2 Images Players and coaches rushed to Egemen Korkmaz after the Turkey U21 boss fell to the floor

Turkey U21 boss Egemen Korkmaz was rushed to hospital after collapsing and falling unconscious on the touchline just seconds after lamenting a refereeing decision.

‌



The 43-year-old fell to the floor 35 minutes into his side's game against Croatia on Tuesday. His colleagues rushed over to him when seemingly slipped and hit his head and, even though Korkmaz had just walked out of shot, camera picked up the worry expressed by coaches and players as they ran over to check on their manager.

‌



An ambulance entered the pitch so that Korkmaz could be treated by paramedics before he was then carried away on a stretcher and rushed to hospital.

‌



The match was suspended as a result as both teams returned to the dressing rooms. There was 12 minutes of added time at the end of the first half.

A statement from the Turkish Football Federation (TFF) read: “Our U21 National Team Head Coach Egemen Korkmaz lost consciousness after slipping and hitting his head on the ground in the 35th minute of today’s UEFA European U21 Championship group qualifying match against Croatia at the Opus Arena in Osijek.

Max Dowman scores sensational solo goal for England as Arsenal youngster takes centre stage READ MORE :

Roberto De Zerbi reveals Tottenham 'ambition' as club make demands clear to new boss READ MORE :

“Korkmaz, who suffered swelling on his head due to the fall, received initial treatment from our medical team on the sidelines. He was conscious and taken to the hospital by ambulance for further examinations. We wish him a speedy recovery and send our best wishes.”

‌



Korkmaz has not lost any matches during Turkey's qualifying campaign for the U21 Euros next year. They are on course to qualify for the first time since 2000. A number of Turkish sides have written to express their concern and wishes him a speedy recovery.

View 2 Images An ambulance entered the pitch to provide medical attention

Super Lig leaders Galatasaray said in a statement: “We extend our get-well wishes to Egemen Korkmaz, the U21 National Team Coach who fell ill and was taken to the hospital during the Croatia U21 – Turkey U21 match, and we hope for his swift recovery.”

Article continues below

Fenerbahce, who sit second in Turkey, said: “Get well soon, Egemen Korkmaz. We regretfully learned that Egemen Korkmaz, the Head Coach of our U21 National Team, fell ill during the match and was taken to the hospital. We extend our get-well wishes to Egemen Korkmaz and hope for his swift recovery.”

Football.title: Man Utd confident of cashing in on Marcus Rashford transfer as Barcelona stance emerges
Football.content:
Man Utd confident of cashing in on Marcus Rashford transfer as Barcelona stance emerges

Marcus Rashford left Manchester United to join Barcelona on loan last summer and a fresh update has emerged about his future

View 2 Images Marcus Rashford could leave Manchester United on a permanent basis this summer (Image: Steve Welsh/PA Wire)

Manchester United reportedly have confidence that they can complete a permanent sale of Marcus Rashford this summer. Rashford expressed a desire to leave Old Trafford last summer and eventually left the club to join Barcelona on a season-long loan.

‌



Rashford has enjoyed an impressive season at Barcelona, scoring 10 goals and providing 13 assists during his time with the La Liga giants. Throughout the season, there has been speculation about whether or not Rashford will join Barcelona on a permanent basis or return to United following the conclusion of his loan spell.

‌



Barcelona hold the option of signing Rashford on a permanent deal for £26million, although recent reports have suggested that the La Liga giants are yet to make a decision regarding the England international’s future. Now, a fresh report from Sky Sports has claimed that United are looking to receive more than £100million from player sales this summer.

‌



Marcus Rashford and Man Utd get another worrying update as club 'welcome' Barcelona offer READ MORE :

Senne Lammens reveals direct message Michael Carrick sent to Man Utd dressing room READ MORE :

Rashford is one of the players that United are looking to part ways with on a permanent basis this summer, with Barcelona still reportedly looking to sign the forward when his loan deal ends. The La Liga giants can sign Rashford for £26m this summer, but there are claims that Barcelona could renegotiate the deal either for a lower fee or for another loan instead.

However, the aforementioned report states that United have no plans to renegotiate with Barcelona over the £26m fee, and are “confident” they could agree a higher fee with another club if necessary. It has also been claimed that United and Rashford are prepared to work in the summer to ensure the England international manages to secure a permanent move away from Old Trafford.

"Of course, what I want is to stay at Barca," Rashford previously told Sport. "It's an end goal, but it's not the reason why I'm training hard and giving it my best.

"The purpose is to win. Barca is a huge, fantastic club, built to win titles."

Football.title: Casemiro reveals family member cried after Man Utd agreed change to his contract
Football.content:
Casemiro reveals family member cried after Man Utd agreed change to his contract

Casemiro is set to leave Manchester United at the end of the season after waiving a contract extension clause, and he has revealed his wife cries over supporter chants

View 2 Images Casemiro is set to leave Manchester United this summer (Image: OLI SCARFF, AFP via Getty Images)

Casemiro has revealed that his wife was moved to tears when Manchester United supporters pleaded for him to stay at Old Trafford for one more season. It follows an agreement with United that saw a clause in his contract scrapped.

‌



The Brazilian, 34, is set to depart the Red Devils when his deal runs out this summer. He arrived at United in a transfer worth up to £70million from Real Madrid in 2022 and has spent the past four years in Manchester, clocking up more than 150 appearances and lifting two major trophies.

‌



This season, Casemiro has been one of United's standout performers. The former Porto man has missed just two matches for the Reds all campaign and has forged a solid partnership with Kobbie Mainoo since Michael Carrick's arrival in mid-January, as he looks to help the club secure a top-four finish.

‌



Man Utd given Sandro Tonali encouragement as Newcastle CEO makes transfer admission READ MORE :

During United's most recent home fixture, a 3-1 victory over Aston Villa, fans chanted 'One more year, one more year Casemiro' after he broke the deadlock for the Red Devils. The midfielder powered home a header from a Bruno Fernandes corner and celebrated in front of the North West corner.

In the aftermath, Casemiro's wife Anna Mariana was left in tears. The midfielder explained: "Well, honestly I feel so happy, especially for the affection from the fans, and the respect they have for me.

"So, it's just gratitude for this love, it is so exciting. I am hoping not to cry on my last day, as it is such a beautiful experience.

‌



FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

View 2 Images Casemiro's wife was emotional over fan support (Image: Lewis Storey, Getty Images)

"My wife already cried, the other day, when the fans were asking for one more year. So, I just want to enjoy it, enjoy all the moments and I will be a United fan for the rest of my life."

‌



Casemiro had a clause in his United contract that would have triggered a one-year extension had he started 35 Premier League matches in his final campaign at the club, a tally he remains on track to reach. However, Casemiro and the club came to an agreement in January to waive the clause during discussions to formally confirm that he would be departing United at the conclusion of the 2025/26 season.

He had been informed by United officials earlier in the season that his contract would not be renewed, but in early 2026 he chose to make the news public, a request to which United duly agreed. Casemiro has just seven matches left in a United shirt, beginning with a Premier League clash against Leeds United on Monday, April 13.

Football.title: Max Dowman scores sensational solo goal for England as Arsenal youngster takes centre stage
Football.content:
Max Dowman scores sensational solo goal for England as Arsenal youngster takes centre stage

Max Dowman's brilliance was again on show as the teenager scored a magnificent solo goal for England's U19s - just weeks after becoming the Premier League's youngest scorer

View 2 Images Max Dowman ran from his own half to score for England's U19s (Image: @n5local)

Max Dowman scored another stunning solo goal as he shone for England's U19s - but their win over Portugal wasn't enough to see them qualify for this year's Euros.

‌



The Arsenal teenage sensation scored one and laid on two assists as the Young Lions ran riot, securing a 6-0 win. Jesse Derry grabbed a brace whilst Ezra Mayers, Shumaira Mheuka and Harry Howell also got in on the act.

‌



The dominant win wasn't enough though as Serbia's victory over Poland means they take top spot in Group 2 to book their place at the tournament.

‌



England's U19s got off to a flying start and only needed four minutes to take the lead as Derry finished past Diogo Ferreira. They would then score five times in the second half with Dowman's effort the pick of the bunch. The 16-year-old recently became the Premier League's youngest ever goalscorer and, not for the first time this year, showed some individual brilliance.

On Tuesday he picked up the ball out on the right, inside his own half, before dribbling past two defenders, travelling all the way to the Portugal 18 yard box and finishing impressively into the corner.

Max Dowman named the two Arsenal stars who have impressed him the most READ MORE :

Thomas Tuchel leaves door open for Max Dowman World Cup call-up READ MORE :

It drew comparisons with a goal he scored in a 4-2 win for Arsenal against Bayern Munich’s U19 side. After picking up the ball on the right he breezed past two players before producing a Maradona spin to evade a third defender, then finishing with a stunning chip over the goalkeeper.

‌



Dowman's stock continues to rise and he recently scored late on in a win for the Gunners over Everton, which saw his name up in lights as he made history. He'd been given several run outs this season, but that was his first goal for Arsenal with the teenager tipped to scale huge heights.

View 2 Images Max Dowman recently made Premier League history with his goal against Everton (Image: Getty)

After the achievement Mikel Arteta said: "I think the decision that you make has to be delivered. You have to see him train every single day, he does it against these defenders who are in my opinion the best in the world." He also added: "It was a moment for him, probably because he doesn’t seem to be phased by the occasion, the opponent or the game."

Article continues below

Dowman has long had the eye of some of Arsenal's leading lights. Martin Odegaard made him take centre stage after a pre-season game, where he had shone. Declan Rice has also been aiding his development with the pair retaining a good working relationship.

Football.title: England confirm Harry Kane injury as Thomas Tuchel lands new headache ahead of World Cup
Football.content:
Harry Kane will not play for England against Japan on Tuesday evening, owing to an issue picked up in training. Elsewhere, Jordan Henderson has returned to Brentford prematurely.

It comes as a major headache for Thomas Tuchel, who has opted not to deploy a true striker for Tuesday's friendly at Wembley. The German head coach has opted for Jordan Pickford in goal, as well as a back line of Ezri Konsa, Nico O'Reilly, Marc Guehi and Ben White.

The Three Lions' midfield is made up of Elliot Anderson and Kobbie Mainoo, while Anthony Gordon, Morgan Rogers, Cole Palmer and Phil Foden feature in attacking roles. The decision not to field and out-and-out striker comes as slightly head-scratching, considering Tuchel has Dominic Solanke on his bench, as well as Marcus Rashford - who can operate through the middle.

Taking to X to reveal the team-sheet, England's official social media account explained the absence of Kane and Henderson. They wrote: "Harry Kane is rested tonight as a precaution having picked up a minor issue in training, but remains with the squad receiving further assessment. Jordan Henderson returned to Brentford ahead of this evening's fixture."

And football fans were quick to question Tuchel's selection in the replies section of the post. One wrote: "Palmer, Foden & Rogers at one go. Interesting. Let's see how that goes."

A second said: "Is Gordon through the middle really our best back up option if Kane gets injured in the WC!?" while a third added: "What a woefully poor side. No centre forward at home to Japan. At Wembley.

"No natural width on the right. A right back who doesn’t really want to be there. This has got 0-1 written all over it. We should be making forward steps this close to a World Cup. We are going backwards."

Video Loading Video Unavailable Click to play Tap to play The video will auto-play soon 8 Cancel Play now

Speaking about the issue ahead of kick-off, meanwhile, Tuchel explained: "Minor injury out of nothing. It just happened. He had to step out of training yesterday after 15 minutes. No chance to be involved, not even today. So he’ll be further assessed now and will be at the stadium to watch."

He added: "It’s serious enough to not be able to play (tonight), so we have to wait for further assessment. Foden plays on the nine. They play a back three so it’s not a bad thing to drop a little back and ask the question to the back three - who steps out and who doesn’t? I encourage Phil to try stuff, to be creative and adventurous."

Joining Solanke and Rashford on the bench is Harry Maguire, Jude Bellingham, Dean Henderson, Dan Burn, Harvey Barnes, Jarrod Bowen, James Garner, James Trafford, Jason Steele, Djed Spence, Tino Livramento and Lewis Hall.

It comes as England were held to a 1-1 draw by Uruguay on Friday night, despite Tuchel securing victory in all of the nation's qualifying games for the 2026 World Cup, having failed to concede a single goal. White opened the scoring on the night with less than 10 minutes on the clock, before Federico Valverde equalised from the penalty spot four minutes into extra time.

It comes as eight players left the England camp following last week's fixture, owing to injury concerns. Aaron Ramsdale, Fikayo Tomori, Dominic Calvert-Lewin and John Stones all dropped out of the squad in the aftermath, as did Adam Wharton, Noni Madueke, Declan Rice and Bukayo Saka.

Image: PA) PA)

Speaking about losing players, Tuchel told the media: "Not disappointed with the players, disappointed with the fact. It's the reality of the season, the reality of the end of March, reality of players involved in more than one competition.

"We have players in camp that have already played more minutes than last season, so there is some concern. The players deserve the mental break from football, and we could see the energy with which they came back to camp in a new environment.

"It helps them go back to clubs and perform. We want them to perform in their clubs, but it is also our last camp before America, so we want to reconnect to our principles. I'm not upset or angry with the players.

"I got the feeling that everyone was desperate to come. Some of the injured players even stayed to do their treatment, that shows they want to be around the group. No one left straight away. It's a good spirit and that's how it should be."

Football.title: Tottenham Supporters' Trust criticises De Zerbi hire over Greenwood comments
Football.content:
Roberto De Zerbi, the new Tottenham head coach on a five-year deal, said last November that Mason Greenwood was a "good guy" who paid a "heavy price" when they were both at Marseille; the Trust says De Zerbi's appointment has the potential to divide the fanbase

The Tottenham Hotspur Supporters' Trust has criticised Roberto De Zerbi's appointment as Spurs head coach over his backing of Mason Greenwood when he was Marseille boss.

De Zerbi's arrival on a five-year contract "raises serious and far-reaching concerns", the group's strongly worded statement says, adding Spurs were directly warned about the "strength of feeling" among fans.

The Trust acknowledges the "immediate priority" is avoiding relegation with Spurs currently one point above the drop zone with seven games to go but says De Zerbi's hiring has the potential to divide the fanbase.

Greenwood joined Marseille from Manchester United in 2024 after charges against him, which included attempted rape and assault, were dropped. Last November, De Zerbi described him as a "good guy" who paid a "heavy price".

He added at the time: "It saddens me what happened in his life because I know a totally different person than the one who was described."

Greenwood was charged in October 2022 with one count of attempted rape, one of controlling and coercive behaviour and another of assault occasioning actual bodily harm over allegations relating to a woman after images and videos were posted online, although the Crown Prosecution Service dropped the charges in February 2023.

The charges against former Manchester United forward Greenwood were dropped because of "a combination of the withdrawal of key witnesses and new material that came to light", which meant there was "no realistic prospect of conviction".

Sky Sports News understands the Spurs board carefully considered and discussed the sentiments around De Zerbi's association with Greenwood during the hiring process and their new head coach is expected to address the issue.

The Trust says De Zerbi's comments about Greenwood "were unnecessary, ill-judged, and deeply offensive to a significant number of supporters".

"We believe these statements, left unchecked, will create a divide among supporters at a time when we all need to be pulling together to back the team," the statement read.

"It is concerning that the club would put us in this position right when the team needs fans the most.

"Fans are rallying behind the 'All Together, Always' initiative, and this appointment places heavy strain on that unity. If those remarks reflect his genuine views, they cast a troubling shadow over the values of the club we love."

The Trust, which advocated a short-term appointment until the end of the season before recruiting a permanent replacement for Igor Tudor during the summer, accused the club of risking eroding confidence in its integrity and ethical standards.

The statement continued: "We fully understand that the immediate priority is to avoid relegation. However, this situation is the result of prolonged strategic failings.

"THST have warned for years that the club was heading in this direction, and the lack of timely, sound decision-making has now left options severely compromised.

"It will take significant effort for many fans to restore their faith in the club's leadership. That process must begin with transparency, accountability and a renewed commitment to the principles that define Tottenham Hotspur."

'Spurs spoke to De Zerbi about fan concerns'

Sky Sports News' chief correspondent Kaveh Solhekol:

"The Tottenham board were aware of the strength of feeling with regards to his appointment and knew some fans would be unhappy about it. They have spoken to Roberto De Zerbi about it.

"It has been addressed behind closed doors and it will be addressed in public as well.

"When De Zerbi has his first press conference, he will address the media's questions and the concerns of the reporters."

Football.title: ECB chief defends England regime over criticism from 'dropped' players
Football.content:
Recent criticism of Rob Key and Brendon McCullum's England regime from active players is a reaction to being dropped, according to England and Wales Cricket Board chief executive Richard Gould.

Jonny Bairstow, Reece Topley and Liam Livingstone have spoken out at their experiences with the national set-up, which is overseen by managing director Key and head coach McCullum.

Livingstone described his time at last year's Champions Trophy as "the worst experience I've had playing cricket", with Topley stating that the Lancashire all-rounder's comments were "a bit kind".

Bairstow, meanwhile, said last week that "you need the care back in the game", adding that "as soon as you are out of the system, you are out of the system".

Topley and Bairstow last played for England in 2024, while Livingstone's most recent appearance came a year ago.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Key joined the Sky Sports Cricket Podcast to look back at the Ashes

Gould said: "When players come out of the England fold, it's difficult for them.

"It's difficult for any player when they get dropped in any sport and they will not agree with the decision. I wouldn't want them to agree with the decision.

"These are competitive men and women seeking to play at the highest standard for as long as they can.

"On the men's side, we've got 28 centrally contracted players. With the women, we've got about 16 centrally contracted players, but there's probably about 300 players who want to play for our England teams.

"We do have to focus our resources on those that are in the teams."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Australian cricket writer Adam Collins joined the Sunday Supplement panel to discuss if McCullum is building the right culture for England to progress

An ECB review into 4-1 Ashes drubbing ended with Key, McCullum and Test captain Ben Stokes retaining their positions despite criticism of the team's preparation, selection and behaviour.

McCullum is currently in his native New Zealand and will rejoin England ahead of their first Test of the summer against the Black Caps on June 4, although Gould was unable to specify his return date.

"I don't know his flight bookings yet. I don't know when he's coming over," he said.

Gould has ruled out trying to persuade the counties to stop signing Australian players in advance of the 2027 Ashes with Stokes describing the willingness to give opponents experience of playing in English conditions ahead of a big series as "odd".

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Paul Farbrace spoke to Sky Sports about McCullum's tenure in charge of the England cricket team and the need to adapt moving forward

"It would be against the law to discriminate against any nationality in terms of playing cricket so, no, there are no policies in place," Gould said.

ECB managing director Rob Andrew added: "The game constantly debates the number of overseas players, the number in the Blast, the number in the County Championship.

"It goes to the bigger value of the county game as well, in terms of helping grow the game. Rob Key might want all the Australians banned from playing, but I don't. It's not something that was discussed during the domestic review.

"The only thing that is discussed periodically is do we have the right number of overseas players playing in our competitions?"

Football.title: Spurs appoint De Zerbi as third head coach of the season
Football.content:
Tottenham have appointed Roberto De Zerbi as their third head coach of the season.

De Zerbi has agreed terms over a five-year contract with Spurs, currently one point above the Premier League's bottom three, which does not include a relegation release clause.

Spurs are fighting to avoid a first top-flight relegation since 1977 in the final seven games of the season.

De Zerbi's appointment "raises serious and far-reaching concerns", says the Tottenham Hotspur Supporters' Trust, because of his backing of Mason Greenwood when he was Marseille head coach.

Sky Sports News understands the Spurs board carefully considered and discussed the sentiments around De Zerbi's association with Greenwood during the hiring process and their new head coach is expected to address the issue.

De Zerbi has more than a week to prepare for his first game, a trip to Sunderland on April 12, live on Sky Sports, and says climbing the table is Spurs' "short-term priority".

The pressure is on to get this appointment right after Igor Tudor's disastrous 44-day spell in which he failed to win a Premier League game. Spurs have moved on three head coaches in the past year.

De Zerbi, who was previously reluctant to take a job before the summer after leaving Marseille, says he was convinced to join Spurs on a "long-term contract" after discussions with the club's leadership.

"Their ambition for the future has been clear - to build a team capable of reaching great achievements, and to do that playing a style of football that excites and inspires our supporters," De Zerbi told the Spurs website.

"I am here because I believe in that ambition and have signed a long-term contract to give everything to deliver it."

Sporting director Johan Lange said Spurs are pleased De Zerbi, their first choice to take over in the summer, has agreed to take on the mantle of keeping them in the Premier League.

"He is one of the most creative and forward-thinking coaches in world football, and brings with him a wealth of experience at the highest level, including in the Premier League," Lange added.

How De Zerbi plans to keep Spurs up

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Michael Bridge and Kaveh Solhekol give their thoughts on Tottenham Hotspur's new head coach Roberto De Zerbi.

Sky Sports News chief correspondent Kaveh Solhekol:

Roberto De Zerbi is up for the challenge. Spurs have seven games to avoid their first relegation since 1977, and he feels it is a massive responsibility to ensure their ever-present Premier League status is preserved.

Sitting just a point above the drop zone, everybody at Tottenham recognises the perilous position they are in.

De Zerbi has made it clear that the sole goal right now is to channel resources into making sure the club stays up. Everything else - building for the long term and restoring Tottenham to the top end of the Premier League - will come later.

The Italian is not buying into the talk that a rebuild and wholesale changes are needed. He is well aware of the strengths of the current squad and believes it needs consistency, a firm goal and a clear path to get out of danger.

Much has been made of De Zerbi's expansive approach, which his former Brighton captain Lewis Dunk said "baffled" the players when he arrived at the club in September 2022.

But it is understood that with Spurs' current predicament, he will not overcomplicate it for the players, instead simplifying the game and tactics in order to maximise returns in the short term.

The 46-year-old believes so many changes before him at Spurs have affected the players, and now it is about fighting for a common cause.

There have also been question marks over his combustibility, considering his exits at Brighton and Marseille after he fell out with the hierarchies.

For De Zerbi, it is a sign of his passion for the job - he makes huge demands of himself, his players, sporting directors and senior executives. He believes challenging each other is the best way to improve and to get the best from everyone.

De Zerbi's appointment has faced concerns from several Spurs fan groups after he backed Mason Greenwood when he was Marseille boss.

It is understood that he expects questions about this when he is presented to the media for the first time.

But ultimately, De Zerbi wants a strong relationship with fans, as he has done at all previous clubs, to help prevent Spurs from dropping into the Championship.

Sky Sports' Paul Merson:

I was quite bullish about Tottenham staying up and then after the Nottingham Forest game [Spurs losing 3-0 at home], you're like, 'Wow. They're in real trouble'.

It just shows you what a big club Tottenham is. I know they're struggling at the moment, but to get someone like De Zerbi, who's a top, top manager. To get him to come to the club just tells you everything about how big Tottenham is. So they've got a chance now.

I don't care how much money he gets. Whatever he gets, if he keeps them up, it's the best money they've ever, ever, ever spent.

He wanted to come in at the start of next season, he's going to come in now. So they have to throw the kitchen sink at him. They have to. They can't afford to go down.

Can De Zerbi deliver required instant results?

Tottenham, who currently sit one point above the relegation zone, are in need of a head coach who can deliver instant results with just seven games left to secure their survival.

De Zerbi has established himself as a coach who instils a possession-based philosophy, creating teams that are praised for their attractive style of football.

However, the Italian's start at Brighton when he took over mid-season in 2022 following Graham Potter's departure would suggest he might struggle to have the required impact.

De Zerbi failed to win any of his first five Premier League games in charge of Brighton, drawing twice and losing three games, albeit facing a tough schedule.

When taking over at Serie A newcomers Benevento mid-season in 2017, De Zerbi's side were praised for the football they played, but were relegated from Italy's top flight.

De Zerbi failed to win any of his first nine games in charge of Benevento.

The Italian also struggled when taking over Palermo mid-season in 2016, winning just one of his 13 games before being sacked less than three months into the job.

Football.title: Police release Woods' arrest report after car crash
Football.content:
Tiger Woods was charged with charged with driving under the influence, property damage and refusal to submit to a lawful test after his car crash on Friday; Martin Country Sheriff's Office released the arrest affidavit on Tuesday, revealing more details of Woods' crash

Tiger Woods had pills in pocket and 'bloodshot' eyes after looking down at his phone before car crash, report reveals

Sheriff John Budensiek confirmed on Friday that Tiger Woods was arrested and charged with driving under the influence after his car was involved in a crash

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player

Tiger Woods told police he was looking down at his phone and changing the radio station before last week's car crash, with pills found in his pocket at the time of his arrest, according to a sheriff's office report.

Woods was arrested for driving under the influence (DUI) after being involved in a car crash in Jupiter Island, Florida on Friday March 27, where his Land Rover rolled over in a collision with a pick-up truck.

An arrest affidavit, released by the Martin Country Sheriff's Office on Tuesday, revealed that Woods told investigators that he didn't realise the truck in front of him had slowed down.

The affidavit also said the 15-time major champion had "bloodshot and glassy eyes", "extremely dilated pupils" and appeared "lethargic and slow" when he failed several field sobriety exercises.

Woods had climbed out of the passenger seat after the crash and was "sweating profusely", with two white pills, identified as hydrocodone - used to treat severe pain - found in his pocket during a search.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Having been arrested on charges of driving under the influence, Paul McGinley believes Tiger Woods needs to focus on his own wellbeing and shouldn't plan to play at the upcoming Masters

The 50-year-old told deputies he had been looking at his phone and fiddling with the radio before he clipped the truck in front of him, causing an estimated $5,000 (£3,770) worth of damage.

Woods had a compression sock over his right knee and told the sheriff about his seven previous back surgeries and 'over 20 operations on his leg', adding that he has a limp and that his ankle seizes while walking.

He walked away unhurt and took a breathalyser test at the scene which returned negative, but refused to submit a urine sample, leading to him being kept in jail for eight hours before being released on bond in the early hours of Saturday morning.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Andrew Coltart discusses how Tiger Woods' car crash will affect his chances of playing at the Masters

Woods was taken to a local hospital for medical clearance before being transported to the Martin County jail, where he declined medical treatment and was held - under Florida law - for the mandatory eight hours.

"I believed that Woods' normal faculties were impaired, and he was unable to safely operate a motor vehicle," the affidavit stated.

Image: Golfer Tiger Woods stands by his overturned vehicle in Jupiter Island on March 27

Woods was charged with driving under the influence with property damage, along for refusal to submit to a lawful urine test. His court date has been arranged on April 23 at 8.30am.

The five-time Masters champion - as of March 31 - remains listed in the field for the opening major of the year, where Rory McIlroy returns as defending champion. Should he feature, it would mark his first appearance in a major since The Open in July 2024.
