Football.title: Kylian Mbappé excited by France’s spectacular attack before World Cup
Football.content:
“It feels strange to be speaking as though I’m one of the old guys, even though I’m not,” said Kylian Mbappé while on France duty this week. As he wraps up his third year as captain and closes in on a century of appearances, the 27-year-old seems to have finally grown comfortable in his position as the team’s leader.

“Nowadays, I fully realise the role the coach and my teammates are expecting me to have,” the forward added. “I was the star of the team in 2022 and in that position everyone concentrates on you and wants to look after you. Now, it’s the opposite. I’m the one who has to look after the others. Some of them were still kids when I was turning professional.”

He may not be the oldest in the squad, but in goalscoring statistics alone the Real Madrid forward is already the elder statesman. If all goes according to plan this summer, Mbappé will overtake Olivier Giroud as his country’s all-time top scorer, with his goal in a 2-1 win against Brazil taking him just one short of the veteran’s tally of 57.

“There’s more talent and potential than in 2022,” the forward added. “Is it a stronger team? We’ll have to see the results, but we can really aim high with this team.” A glance at the depth of attacking options at Didier Deschamps’ disposal confirms that sentiment, not least given that two entirely different forward lines delivered on their promise over the past week.

While finding a Giroud-like foil to Mbappé once seemed to be the key to unlocking France’s attack, that concern has been rendered irrelevant through the sheer quantity of talent gravitating around the captain. With Ousmane Dembélé, Michael Olise and Rayan Cherki propelling the team’s transitions, Les Bleus are rarely short of invention in the final third.

France played with an impressive freedom in the attacking third. It was Dembélé, deployed in a role oscillating between midfield and wing, who played Mbappé through for the opener against the Seleção. Hugo Ekitike added a second, finishing off a counterattack after drifting into the middle. Nominally the central playmaker, Michael Olise enjoyed a similar freedom to roam across the frontline. Despite Dayot Upamecano’s red card, and a late goal from Carlo Ancelotti’s men from defender Gleison Bremer, France saw out their first win against Brazil since 2011.

In their second match, a 3-1 win against Colombia in Maryland, Désiré Doué swept in his first goal for Les Bleus. Marcus Thuram then ended an international goalscoring drought that had stretched back to 2023 by heading in a cross from Monaco’s Maghnes Akliouche, finally overtaking his father’s international tally of two goals in the process. The Inter striker was again involved for the third goal, setting up Doué after a rapid counterattack.

View image in fullscreen Désiré Doué and Marcus Thuram both scored in France’s 3-1 win against Colombia. Photograph: Hannah Foslien/Getty Images

Although defence was a secondary concern this week, a spate of misplaced passes and missed tackles over the two matches hinted at an increasing fragility at the back. It was Maxence Lacroix, who earned his first cap against Colombia, who was the most assured of France’s defenders over the week. While he was only called up this month as a replacement for William Saliba, the Crystal Palace defender took his chance decisively and staked his claim for a spot in the World Cup squad.

In any case, the main objective of France’s trip was for the squad to find their bearings in Boston, with the downtown Four Seasons hotel set to serve as their base camp the summer. The venue for their match against Brazil, in the outskirts of the Massachusetts capital, will also host their group stage match against Norway this summer.

While the squad was largely shielded from any political questions this month, the delegation did flag up a few logistical issues. More than the stadiums or training facilities, the main concerns revolved around the traffic jams in town and the waiting times at the airport. “We spent so long at the airport when we arrived,” Deschamps lamented in his press conference after the team touched down in Washington before playing Colombia in Maryland. “I’ve never seen those kinds of checks. We’ll adapt to it.”

The head coach also complained about the mid-March cooling break. “If you have momentum, those three minutes break it up,” he said in his post-Brazil conference. “It’s not ideal if a team is on the verge of breaking down their opponent, and it turns into a match with four quarters. I guess the broadcasters are happy, though.”

View image in fullscreen Hugo Ekitike scored in the 2-1 win against Brazil. Photograph: Guilherme Veiga/PX Imagens/ZUMA Press Wire/Shutterstock

The prevailing mood in the France camp is nevertheless an optimistic one. That said, Les Bleus will be all too aware from past experiences that possessing a wealth of attacking talent does not guarantee a successful World Cup.

Their opener against Senegal will inevitably call up memories of the group stage in 2002, when a team that featured the top goalscorers from Europe’s top leagues crashed out unceremoniously. More recently, a World Cup-winning France squad to which the returning Karim Benzema was added failed to reach the Euro 2020 quarter-finals.

For the time being, though, Mbappé’s assessment of the current squad’s strength has not been disproved. While Deschamps is seemingly yet to settle on his World Cup squad, let alone a first-choice XI, the ease with which his forwards combined with each other around the captain is a positive sign before the final act of his 14-year spell in charge.

“I’m well aware that there are some very good players that I won’t be bringing because, in my opinion, there are even better ones,” warned the 57-year-old after the Colombia match. With several other in-form forwards waiting in the wings, from an injured Bradley Barcola to a rejuvenated Florian Thauvin, a place France’s supporting cast will not come cheaply.

This is an article by Get French Football News

News.title: Dozens of hooded youngsters flood high street shops in broad daylight with stores closing early & cops rushing to scene
News.content:
LAWLESS youths are continuing to run wild looting businesses along Clapham High Street – as cops flank the road and close shops early.

Shocking clips shared on social media show crowds of feral teens tearing through the neighbourhood and terrorising locals in South London.





The Marks and Spencer Food Hall on the high street – which was looted by a similar flash mob over the weekend leading to two arrests – has shut early amid fears of being targeted by the yobs again.

Waitrose, Sainsbury’s and McDonald’s, have now also been forced to close as officers work to bring the situation under control.

Flailing cops are heavily outnumbered by the vast swathes of youths unleashing havoc – as they desperately try to chase the youngsters away.

The Daily Mail reports that terrified families are “barricaded” inside a local Sainsbury’s as youths continue to claim control of the busy high street.



The paper adds that a local Waitrose has also apparently closed its doors too.

Traffic was forced to come to a standstill as the yobs, in their droves, filled the road.

Cops desperately tried to break the vast group but most of the yobs appeared to hold their ground.

A Metropolitan Police spokesperson said: “Police are responding to an ongoing incident on Clapham High Street following reports of a large crowd of young people causing anti-social behaviour.



“Officers are on the scene, and a dispersal order has been put in place, meaning anyone congregating must leave the area.

“At this time two teenage girls have been arrested on suspicion of assaulting an emergency worker. They have been taken to custody.

“Officers will remain in the area to offer support and respond to any concerns from local residents and businesses.”

The latest chaos follows ugly scenes that saw a wild mob of youths run riot in a M&S store and terrorise the streets of Clapham on Saturday.

The meet up and carnage is said to have been pre arranged online.



Officers were forced to issue a dispersal order and two 16-year-old girls.

One 15-year-old girl was arrested for shoplifting and assault during the mass gathering of over 100 teens.

More than 20 youths are seen shoving each other in the frozen food aisle while the police officers attempt to quell the chaos by gently breaking up the group.

Lots of the youths are hooded or wearing hats.

The cops have little impact and many more teens stand on the side watching or filming the ordeal.



One girl even appears to be crying but ignores the policeman who tries to assist her.

Eventually the riot disbands and the police officers usher the youngsters out the shop.

The mob were understood to be targeting several other shops in the area.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

The footage from Saturday’s carnage has since gone viral on social media and users have branded it an example of lawless London.

MORE TO FOLLOW…

News.title: Russian drone impales craft mid-air in combat dubbed ‘drone jousting’ as Vlad sends Ukraine’s craft at its own allies
News.content:
RUSSIAN drone interceptors have been impaling Ukrainian UAVs mid-air in an unprecedented form of sky combat dubbed “jousting”.

Vladimir Putin has also been diverting Ukrainian drones towards the Baltic states – in a desperate bid to make it look like Kyiv is striking its allies.





Flying devices armed with sharp metal rods to stab Ukrainian aircraft have been seen in gob-smacking footage downing targets.

One clip appears to show one of the new Russian aircraft hurtling down before attaching to a Ukrainian Darts-type loitering strike drone.

It stabs down on the Ukrainian craft’s topside before burning its battery.

The target then falls towards the ground while in flames following the mid-air attack.

Similar first-person-view videos recorded from the jousting devices also show other successful and unsuccessful interception attempts.

On several occasions, the Russian interceptor appears to remain completely intact after downing the Ukrainian targets.

Many Ukrainian drones use wings made of polystyrene or foam as it reduces production costs.

But this makes them easy to destroy as their thin skin is vulnerable to piercing.



Other interceptor drones have been seen deploying trident-like rods to thrust through enemy UAVs.

Meanwhile, Putin has also been diverting Ukrainian drones so that they target the Baltic states and other European allies.

Using electronic warfare, Moscow has been tampering with drones mid-flight so that they re-direct to target countries including Finland and Estonia.

Ukrainian foreign minister Andrii Sybiha said that Kyiv has never fired drones towards the Baltic states.

He also said Ukraine was working hard to ensure these occurrences never happen again.



Sybiha said: “I can state with confidence that in all these cases, these were entirely deliberate and targeted actions by Russia.

“The available intelligence data indicates that Russia has been intentionally diverting drones to the Baltic states in order to use these incidents for its information purposes.

“I am grateful to all our partners, the Baltic states and also Finland, who together with us are stating clearly that the cause of these incidents lies with Russia.



“It is Russia’s war that created all these threats, and it is Russia that has to be forced into peace.”

Three stray Ukrainian drones were found in Finland over the last few days – but no injuries were reported in each case.

In Estonia, another alleged Ukrainian craft was found on Tuesday.



It comes as Putin continues to rake in profits from the war in Iran – while also helping the regime strike US-Israeli targets.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Volodymyr Zelensky has claimed that Russia is mapping out US assets in the Middle East – in an alliance with Iran that helped blow up a spy plane worth £700million.

Citing Ukrainian intelligence, the Zelensky accused the Kremlin of sharing satellite images ahead of Iranian bombardments of an American base in Saudi Arabia.

News.title: BBC apologises after failing to act on Scott Mills allegation after it was raised with broadcaster last year
News.content:
BEEB bosses have apologised after failing to act on an allegation against Scott Mills after it was reportedly raised with the broadcaster last year.

The former Radio 2 host, 53, was quizzed by cops in 2018 over separate allegations of “serious sexual offences” against a boy under 16.





The case – said to have taken place between 1997 and 2000 – was later dropped in full due to a lack of evidence.

And it was revealed yesterday that Mills had been fired from his Radio 2 Breakfast Show over allegations surrounding his “personal conduct.”

But it has since been reported that BBC chiefs were contacted almost a year ago by former presenter Anna Brees, who raised concerns about Mills.

She contacted the Beeb in May 2025 after receiving information about separate alleged “inappropriate communications” involving the Radio 2 DJ.

According to The Telegraph, the ex-BBC host questioned whether any “formal or informal complaints” had been received about Mills.

Her query related to “safeguarding, inappropriate conduct or harassment”, the outlet said.

She also asked whether the broadcaster had ever conducted an internal investigation into him, but did not receive a response.

The BBC admitted her information “should have been followed up and we should have asked further questions”.



In a statement, the Beeb said: “We received a press query in 2025 which included limited information.

“This should have been followed up and we should have asked further questions.

“We apologise for this and will look into why this did not happen.

“More broadly, we would always urge anyone who has concerns or information to raise it with us.”

Her inquiries do not relate to the same alleged victim whose complaint to the police led to Mills being questioned in 2018.



Mills began at Radio 1 in 1998 presenting the early morning slot before earning his own namesake programme The Scott Mills Show.

He took over the Radio 2 flagship breakfast show in January 2025 from Zoe Ball.

But yesterday, an internal message was sent around Radio 2 after Mills’ exit was made public.

Lorna Clarke, Director of Music at the BBC, confirmed the sacking in a statement to staff.



It read: “I wanted to personally let you know that Scott Mills has left the Breakfast show, and the BBC.

“I know that this news will be sudden and unexpected and therefore must come as a shock.

“Not least as so many of us have worked with Scott over a great many years, across a broad range of our programmes on R1, 5Live, R2 and TV.

“I felt it was important to share this news with you at the earliest opportunity.”

The BBC has not given any further details over the allegations and it is not clear what, if any, role the police investigation played in his sacking.



News of Mills’ dismissal was reportedly not briefed to his production team.

Last Tuesday was the final time Mills – who earns almost £360,000 with the broadcaster – was on air.

Blindsided by the sacking, the presenter signed off just like every other as he looked forward to the next day’s broadcast – which never came.

After talking with Vernon Kay, Scott told listeners: “I’m back tomorrow, with Buffy The Vampire Slayer. Thank you!”

RECOMMENDED STORIES

However, Gary Davies stood in the following day as he was joined by Jason Manford, with the DJ filling in for each show since.



Davies, who has been confirmed as the stand in for Scott for the foreseeable future, came on air to tell fans he was “in for Scott Mills”.

News.title: World War Two veteran dies aged 100 — after received over 16,000 cards for his milestone birthday
News.content:
A WORLD War Two veteran has died at the age of 100 — after receiving more than 16,000 cards for his landmark birthday last year.

Dougie Shelley, who joined the Royal Navy at 17 and served in the Arctic convoys, died on March 21.





He was a seaman gunner on the destroyer HMS Milne on D-Day — guarding troops going ashore ­during the Normandy landings in June 1944.

He was in the Far East at the end of the war, and described those who survived to celebrate as “lucky fellas”.

After the war, Dougie worked on ships taking Ten Pound Poms to Australia.

He later became a ­Ministry of Defence driver.

He was sent 16,266 birthday messages on his centenary last September.

The messages included one from King Charles and Queen Camilla.

Dougie, of Southend, Essex, also learned he would receive France’s highest accolade, the Legion d’Honneur.

Capt Bill Oliphant, of the Royal Naval ­Association, said: “Our Second World War veterans are the last voices of this period in history.”

News.title: Scott Mills was dropped like a hot cake, but something doesn’t add up – what evidence does Beeb have?
News.content:
MATHS has never really been my strong suit, but something about the Scott Mills scandal doesn’t quite add up.

For those in blissful ignorance, 53-year-old Mills has been unceremoniously sacked from the flagship Radio 2 breakfast show and, despite the BBC’s failure to explain why, it’s reportedly linked to historic allegations of “serious sexual offences” against a teenage boy.





Except that the alleged offences took place around 29 years ago, were investigated by police ten years ago, and no action was taken because there was a lack of evidence.

So what evidence does the BBC have now that the police and Crown Prosecution Service didn’t?

With little confirmed information available at the time of writing, it’s tricky to grasp exactly what’s gone on here.

But some insiders have suggested he was actually sacked for breach of contract because he didn’t disclose to the BBC that he’d been investigated.

Hmmm. We now know the BBC was aware.

He remained on Radio One from the time he was grilled in July 2018 to May 2019, when prosecutors decided not to bring charges.

BBC chiefs are refusing to give any further information on why it axed Mills, or what had changed since their original decision to do nothing.

Look, if Mills was found guilty of behaving inappropriately with a teenage boy when he himself was in his early twenties, then you’d find no defence of that from me.





But he wasn’t.

Prosecutors decided that the accusation couldn’t be proved “beyond reasonable doubt” and, unless new evidence has come to light, that should have been the end of the matter.

Instead, it seems that the original complainant might have watched the Channel 5 drama about the BBC’s Huw Edwards scandal and felt motivated to come forward again.

And consequently, a BBC rattled by criticism of its handling of allegations against both newsreader Edwards and DJ Jimmy Savile, dropped Mills like a hot cake.

So as it stands, it appears the only thing that’s changed is the climate at the BBC and other risk-averse corporations.

Now, HR departments seem to act as judge and jury in deciding that their “balance of probability” outweighs the CPS’s evidential “beyond reasonable doubt” test if there’s a danger of reputational harm to a company or institution.

Whatever happened to innocent until proven guilty?

Mills had wanted to be a DJ from the age of 11, but now his long career lies in ruins.

Whether the punishment fits the alleged crime remains to be proven.



AMERICA’S FBI director Kash Patel has suffered an “embarrassing” breach of security after hackers got in to his personal account and published photos of his family holiday.

That the accounts of someone of his supposed security level can be breached takes a level of computer know-how that’s baffling to technophobic old me.

Most of the time, I can’t even access my own accounts.

ROYAL HOUSE PESTS

PRINCE Harry has let it be known through the “friends” he claims never talk to the press that he and Meghan would relish an invitation to join the King at Sandringham this summer.

One can only imagine how this has gone down in the royal household.

How does one tell one’s son that one is too busy to accommodate them for one’s entire month’s break?

Tricky. And if the invite stiffy does get sent, the potential problems are endless.

What’s the betting Charles will be equipped with a chest-mounted GoPro to avoid any more “recollections may vary” misunderstandings?

And will Camilla be swiftly dispatched to Hobbycraft to stock up on hessian drawstring pouches, papier-mache hearts, and crown-shaped cookie cutters to make the guest bedroom a welcoming space for her exacting step-daughter-in-law?



As for William and Kate, something tells me they’ll suddenly find urgent business to attend to overseas.

STRICTLY bosses are reportedly “in talks” with comedian Miranda Hart about taking over from Claudia Winkleman.

Is there anyone they’re not supposedly in talks with?

FERGIE FLITS

THEY seek her here, they seek her there, they seek her everywhere.

Is she is heaven? Is she in hell?

That damned elusive Ginger Pimpernel.

Sarah Ferguson’s exact location is unknown but speculation suggests she could be anywhere from the Middle East and Canada, to Asia or Donegal.

Wherever she is, what’s the betting that someone else is paying for it?

SIR KEIR, A NATURAL YAWN LEADER



AMERICAN comedian WC Fields once advised that you should never work with children or animals because of their unpredictability.

So, whatever possessed Sir Keir Starmer to give a droning speech about screen time at a South London primary school?

I think it’s fair to say that the pictured pupils speak for us all.

DULL BEATS DUMB

KEVIN BERESFORD, aka Britain’s “dullest man” famous for his calendars of car parks, says he’s taking on the “manosphere” with a rival ‘dullosphere’ for young men.

“It’s now sexy being dull,” says the 73-year-old from Redditch in Worcestershire.

Except that, for any woman who knows her worth, the manosphere lot are already categorised as mind-numbingly dumb.

They’re self (and selfie) obsessed, spend way too long in the gym, live in a toxic bubble, and bore on for centuries about their wants/needs/views etc with little regard for those of others.

A car-park calendar would be fascinating by comparison.



HAVING kids doesn’t necessarily make us happier, says a new study.

In fact, whether we have them or not has little bearing on our “eudaimonic wellbeing”, whatever that is.

Did we need a study to tell us this? The bottom line is that, if you’re a fundamentally happy or unhappy person, then you’ll probably remain so irrespective of whether you have a child or not.

But one thing I can say for sure is that, while the early years of parenting are exhausting and full of sacrifices, hanging out with my now-adult children is undoubtedly when I’m at my happiest.

News.title: How Putin is trying to flood UK with migrants by luring them with cheap flights before dumping them on Polish border
News.content:
RUSSIAN tyrant Vladimir Putin is sending migrants to Britain after teaming up with people traffickers in his war with the West.

The Kremlin dictator’s goons are luring desperate asylum seekers from Africa and the Middle East to Russia and puppet state Belarus with offers of cheap flights and visas.





But when they arrive, they are instead beaten and herded to Belarus’s border with Poland to drive them into the EU and onwards, often, to the UK.

At least 28,000 illegal crossing attempts were made from Belarus to Poland last year.

And while Putin is being buoyed by an increase in oil revenue for his country due to the war in Iran, he is out to maximise Europe’s migrant chaos to destabilise his enemies and hurt their economies.

Belarus’s border with Poland is a frozen wilderness fortified with two rows of fencing stretching 115 miles and topped by razor wire.

The area is patrolled by more than 2,300 border guards, backed by surveillance cameras and drones.

But traumatised refugees told The Sun how they were attacked and forced across the border by Belarusian thugs — or signed up for Russia’s meatgrinder war if they failed to reach Poland.

Somali TV producer Ilyas Elmi, 45, fled to Russia after being warned he was on a rebel hit list in the nation’s bloody civil war. He was granted a tourist visa to board a cheap flight to Moscow.





Ilyas had planned to use people smugglers to help him cross into Poland, before making his way to see his wife and child in Germany.

Horror stories

But, instead, he found himself part of 13-strong group bused to the remote forested border area inhabited by wolves, bears and herds of wild bison.

There, Belarusian guards beat him and ordered him to cross an 18ft steel fence topped with razor wire at the Polish frontier.

Ilyas told The Sun: “They wouldn’t let us turn back and told me they would shoot me dead if I tried. We ended up starving there for 40 days and nights.

“There were four women in my group and one of them, she was called Nadia and 22 years old, got so sick she died.

“The guards ordered us back into the forest when we tried to get her to hospital.”

Ilyas survived and managed to sneak back into Russia before being arrested trying to reach the border with Finland.

He was thrown into a jail in St Petersburg to await deportation.

But he was then handed a document written in Russian to sign and promised he could stay if he agreed to work for the government for 12 months.

Trembling as he recalled his ordeal, he said: “I asked them what kind of work it would be and they said it would be cleaning, driving or perhaps gardening so I signed.



“But I was then put in a van with other migrants and driven for two days and two nights until it stopped at an army camp near the Ukraine border.

“I was horrified when I realised they had lied and told them I would refuse to fight. I said I preferred to die in Somalia than fighting for Russia.”

Ilyas managed to use his TV contacts to report his plight to authorities and escaped the likely death sentence of the war before being allowed to make an asylum application in Poland.

But he has lost touch with Somali, Syrian and Yemeni travelling companions who wound up on the front line — including one who was later captured by Ukrainian forces.

Now living in the Polish city of Bialystok near the Belarus border, Ilyas said: “I know I’m very lucky but I also know that many have died trying to reach Poland.

“Many more are getting across the border illegally and travelling further west. I have four of five Somali friends who made it to the UK and are safe there now.”

Horror stories of Belarusian brutality have emerged from Polish sources since the eastern route opened in 2021 just before the start of the Ukraine war.

Migrants are said to have lost feet to frostbite in winter after guards took away their shoes.



Many more are getting across the border illegally and travelling further west. I have four of five Somali friends who made it to the UK and are safe there now Somali Ilyas Elmi

And others, gasping with thirst, have been given water containers laced with broken glass. Guards following Kremlin orders to maximise the exodus have bused tens of thousands to the forbidding frontier.

The Belarusians regularly cut holes in the fence and batter terrified migrants with batons while pushing them into Poland.

Others have been forced to climb over the barrier and suffered serious injuries caused by falls and razor wire.

Putin’s Belarusian henchmen have also built at least four tunnels under the frontier, reportedly aided by experts from Russia’s Hamas allies, who built Gaza’s underground network.

The most sophisticated — a Great Escape-style construction unearthed in December last year — had concrete supports in a 5ft-high crawl space stretching 70 metres. Polish border officers rounded up 130 arrivals who came through it but 50 more vanished and are believed to have linked up with smugglers to head west.

They keep moving because Poland offers no UK-style welcome blanket or the promise of a free hotel or healthcare.

They immediately find themselves hunted by Polish border guards with orders to push them straight back, with the nation having passed laws banning asylum claims a year ago.

Videos have shown desperate arrivals being pepper-sprayed and teargassed on the Polish side and returned back into the clutches of Belarusians, who beat them again.



Huge resources have been spent on guard patrols and border security as more than 13,000 migrants were pushed back in the past 12 months.

On both sides of the frontier, more than 100 bodies have been found frozen to death or drowned in treacherous marshes around the Bug River, which makes up part of the border.

The Polish government has been forced to spend £325million on the huge border fence, completed in June 2023, and millions more on patrols.

‘Broken bones’

Poles are convinced that Belarusian president Aleksandr Lukashenko and his officials are actively encouraging people smuggling and are even in league with the gangs.

The campaign is low-cost for Belarus yet leaves Poland and other EU nations with millions less to spend on arms for Ukraine. Russia and Belarus have been using social media to advertise enticing travel packages and easy EU access for those in strife-torn third world nations, promising “you will feel safe”.

Sudanese migrant Youssef, a 27-year-old electronics technician from Khartoum — whose name we changed at his request — fell for one of the ads and fled his nation’s civil war in May last year.

He was granted a 12-month visa to study at the university in Belarusian capital Minsk and a flight costing £520 after making contact with helpful go-betweens in the puppet state.

But after three months the visa was revoked. He was arrested and jailed and then found himself being bused to the border with Poland.

He was then almost beaten to death by Belarusians after being pushed back and forth over the border three times in July last year.

I want to stay in Poland now and try to live in safety here but there are many more coming in illegally who are heading further west Youssef

Slightly-built and softly-spoken Youssef said: “They took me and others like me to a hole they had cut in the fence and smashed us with batons as they pushed us through.



“I was so terrified I gashed my leg crawling through the razor wire and was in a terrible state.

“The Poles didn’t beat me but pushed me back, then the Belarusians attacked me again and sent me back through another hole.

“Others were in an even worse state with broken bones after being made to climb the fence and jump.

“The last time I crossed I was going to die but the Poles finally took pity on me and took me to hospital.”

Youssef is one of the lucky few Poland has allowed to claim asylum in recent months. Claims are limited to those with serious medical conditions, pregnant women and unaccompanied minors.

Youssef wept as he added: “I buried the remains of my girlfriend, my grandmother and my aunt after they were blown up by a rebel bomb in Khartoum and I shiver at the thought of ever going back.

“But I’m every bit as scared of going back to Belarus. There are terrible people there who care nothing for human life.

“I want to stay in Poland now and try to live in safety here but there are many more coming in illegally who are heading further west.

“The Russians and Belarusians don’t care how much we suffer — they are just using us.”

Lieutenant Katarzyna Zdanowicz, of the Polish Border Force, which now runs stations and watchtowers along the border, told The Sun: “There is no question that the Russians are engineering this crisis.



“Who else would organise so many crossing attempts and even dig professional tunnels under the border?

“It is impossible not to feel sorry for the people trying to cross.

“We try to treat them humanely, but our orders are to push them back unless they are very sick, pregnant or young.

“Winter is normally our quiet time but we know the crossing will begin again soon, but we are ready and appreciate the importance of our work.

“A secure border here protects not only Poland, but the whole of Europe.”

News.title: Moment Brit warship crew scramble to intercept Putin sub ‘at risk of EXPLODING’ as it’s tracked through English Channel
News.content:
THIS is the stunning moment a Brit warship scrambles to intercept a Russian sub in the English Channel amid fears it could explode.

Astonishing footage showed HMS Iron Duke tracking Vladimir Putin‘s menacing Novorossiysk sub sneaking towards UK waters.





Concerns were mounting that the 230ft vessel could explode after a fuel leak in the Strait of Gibraltar, before it steamed towards the UK.

So the navy crew tracked the sub, carrying 50 people, to gather intel – and make sure it didn’t cause a blast in British seas.

Jaw-dropping footage showed the crew spotting the submarine, visible above water, with their binoculars.

In the clip, the warship scrambles after being instructed to “investigate unknown contact”.

The team declares that they are just seven nautical miles from the Russian vessel.

“We’ve definitely got her”, one mariner declares, before the captain makes a dramatic announcement.

He says: “Listen in lads, do you hear the Captain speaking?



“We have been tracking a Russian submarine that’s departed the Mediterranean as tracked by our own Gibraltar squadron, and is assessed as heading back towards UK waters.

“We had a call earlier today from the Maritime Operations Centre telling us to intercept the Russian submarine and shadow it as it transits through UK waters.”

“We’ll of course keep you posted as the situation develops and as the timeline unfolds.”

The Novorossiysk, which came into service in 2014, did not have a nuclear reactor on board at the time of the daring interception.

But it was part of a group of submarines that carry Kalibr cruise missiles.



The Royal Navy tracked the vessel over three days, from October 7 to 9.

HMS Iron Duke and a Wildcat helicopter from 825 Naval Air Squadron were scrambled to follow the Russian tyrant’s sub.

As Putin’s ship hurtled towards its target, Storm Amy hit the region and threatened to torpedo the mission.



This forced the Dutch navy to take over and escort the submarine and an accompanying towing vessel, the Yakov Grebelsky, in the North Sea.

They were later returned home to St Petersburg in Russia.

The Novorossiysk can operate at a depth of nearly 1,000ft and has a range of 7,500 nautical miles.

At the time of the mission, Nato chief Mark Rutte ridiculed Moscow over the “limping” condition of Putin’s subs.

Growing trend of Russian spying on British soil By Mike Sullivan A counter-terrorism chief has warned of the growing trend of Russia using criminal proxies to spy on British soil. Commander Dominic Murphy, the head of the Metropolitan Police Counter-Terrorism Command vowed never to take his “eye off the ball” as he hailed his team’s success. He said: “This is one of the largest and most complex examples of a group working for a foreign state to conduct intelligence surveillance operations here in the UK so it is a very significant case and I am very proud of the investigation team and the success they have had. “This investigation uncovered spying on behalf of the Russian state on an industrial case, in this case committed by a group of Bulgarians contracted by an individual to conduct that spying on behalf of Russia. “As the UK becomes a more hostile environment as a result of our work we will see them increasingly use proxies to conduct their activities.” The ring was smashed in raids on properties in London and ringleader Orlin Roussev’s address in Great Yarmouth in February 2023, where police uncovered a treasure trove of hi-tech spyware. On the challenges faced by enemy states operating on UK soil, he said: “Within counter-terrorism policing we are seeing more than 20% of our demand now coming from threat posed from foreign states to our national security so this is an ever growing challenge for us. “We are committed to working closely with intelligence agencies in this country and our international partners to disrupt activity by foreign states. “We have been working hard to make the UK a hostile working operating environment for these countries and this is an example of that because this group were contracted to operate on behalf of Russian intelligence services because this is a hostile environment for them to operate in directly here. “So some positives but we will never take our eye off the ball working with our partners to keep the UK safe.”

Russia‘s Black Sea Fleet claimed the diesel-powered Novorossiysk had surfaced off France in order to comply with navigation rules in the English Channel.



Russia rejected reports the hulking vessel had suffered a serious malfunction.

According to VChK-OGPU, a Telegram channel known for publishing Russian security leaks, fuel was leaking into the hold of the Novorossiysk as of September 27 – raising the risk of a blast.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

The dramatic clip is part of the first episode of the new series of Channel 5‘s “Warship: Life in the Royal Navy” – which airs on Wednesday at 8pm.

Ex-Royal Marine JJ Chalmers and Kate Humble present the show focusing on life on board HMS Iron Duke with a 200-strong crew.

News.title: Historic piece of the Eiffel Tower goes up for sale & could be yours… if you can find somewhere to fit it in your house
News.content:
PIECE OF PARIS Historic piece of the Eiffel Tower goes up for sale & could be yours… if you can find somewhere to fit it in your house

AFTER overlooking Paris for 139 years and surviving two major world wars, a piece of an iconic landmark will be sold to one lucky buyer.

In just months, a fragment of the original Eiffel Tower steps will go to auction.





Standing 1,083 feet tall, construction on the famed tower began in January 1887.

It has since become a major attraction in the City of Love, drawing millions of visitors every year.

Super fans will now have the opportunity to have a piece of the tower in their home.

Slated to be auctioned off on May 21, Paris-based Artcurial Auction will host the sale of the historic item.

The spiral staircases that cascaded from the second and third floors were removed in 1983 and replaced with elevators.

Split into 24 different sections, one is now located on the first floor of the Eiffel Tower.

Three other pieces can be found in Iron Museum, Musée d’Orsay and La Villette – all located in Paris.



The piece set for auction is 8.5 feet tall.

Its anonymous owner has decided to sell the item after holding it in their private collections for four decades.

The staircase has an estimated value of between £34,700 and £43,400 (€40,000 and €50,000).

Consisting of 14 steps that stem from its cross-shaped base, it is made from steel and riveted sheet metal.

Sabrina Dolla, a specialist from Artcurial’s Art Deco, spoke to Artnet about the owner’s decision to sell the piece.



“He’s enjoyed it long enough and now his circumstances are taking him elsewhere,” she said.

Dolla said smaller sections of the staircase sell better as buyers are able to fit them into most areas inside their homes.

The auction house has previously sold other sections of the staircase from the Eiffel Tower.

In 2013, one piece was sold for £184,000 (€212,458).

Section 13 also sold for a huge £454,800 (€523,800) in 2016, while section four was sold for £141,100 (€162,500).



RECOMMENDED STORIES

The last piece to be sold was section 17, which was purchased for £220,100 (€253,500).

News.title: Donald Trump's fury as ballroom blitzed by judge in humiliation for US President
News.content:
Donald Trump's fury as ballroom blitzed by judge in humiliation for US President

The Trump ballroom is a major, nearly half-a-billion-dollar plan that the US President claims is a more economical project than simply restoring the White House East Wing

View 4 Images Donald Trump's plans for a White House ballroom have been dealt a major blow

Donald Trump has been dealt a humiliating blow by a federal judge who has ruled the US President has "no authority" over one of his centrepiece projects.

‌



A US judge has halted construction on Trump's White House ballroom construction project after finding proper procedures were not followed before the project began. Judge Richard Leon, a Republican appointee, decided the President does not have "the authority he claims to have" in the wake of a lawsuit put forward by The National Trust for Historic Preservation.

‌



The judge wrote: "I have concluded that the National Trust is likely to succeed on the merits because no statute comes close to giving the President the authority he claims to have."

‌



OPINION Voice of the Mirror 'Sending King Charles to the White House is a risk the UK does NOT need to take'

View 4 Images Cranes being used to build the new ballroom could be seen over the White House (Image: AP)

"The President of the United States is the steward of the White House for future generations of First Families. He is not, however, the owner!" Construction of the ballroom, part of the President's long running bid to make over the White House complex to his own tastes, was launched late last year, and is a major, $400 million (£302 million) plan expected to turn out a new 90,000 square foot building.

‌



The ruling adds to what has been a stressful week for Trump, who has been taking to social media to complain about his "war of choice" in Iran, as he is no closer to decapitating a regime nearly a month after launching into strikes alongside Israel.

Early on Tuesday morning, the President made a pointed post on his Truth Social platform pointing a finger at the UK and France for failing to back the conflict - which is having profound economic consequences on the global economy. The President reacted in a similar vein to today's decision, branding the National Trust for Historic Preservation "a radical left group of lunatics whose funding was stopped by Congress in 2005".

View 4 Images The Trump ballroom project is set to cost up to $400 million (Image: AP)

‌



In another long Truth Social rant, he complained: "The National Trust for Historic Preservation sues me for a Ballroom that is under budget, ahead of schedule, being built at no cost to the Taxpayer, and will be the finest Building of its kind anywhere in the World.

"I then get sued by them over the renovation of the dilapidated and structurally unsound former Kennedy Center, now, The Trump Kennedy Center (A show of Bipartisan Unity, a Republican and Democrat President!), where all I am doing is fixing, cleaning, running, and 'sprucing up' a terribly maintained, for many years, Building, but a Building of potentially great importance.

"Yet, The National Trust for Historic Preservation, a Radical Left Group of Lunatics whose funding was stopped by Congress in 2005, is not suing the Federal Reserve for a Building which has been decimated and destroyed, inside and out, by an incompetent and possibly corrupt Fed Chairman."

Article continues below

View 4 Images Trump raged at the decision in a post on Truth Social (Image: Getty Images)

"The once magnificent Building is BILLIONS over budget, may never be completed, and may never open. All of the beautiful walls inside have been ripped down, never to be built again, but the National “Trust” for Historic Preservation never did anything about it!

"Or, have they sued on Governor Gavin Newscum’s 'RAILROAD TO NOWHERE' in California that is BILLIONS over Budget and, probably, will never open or be used. So, the White House Ballroom, and The Trump Kennedy Center, which are under budget, ahead of schedule, and will be among the most magnificent Buildings of their kind anywhere in the World, gets sued by a group that was cut off by Government years ago, but all of the many DISASTERS in our Country are left alone to die. Doesn’t make much sense, does it? President DONALD J. TRUMP"

News.title: UK snow maps show 3 cities face flurries in Easter weekend forecast – full list
News.content:
UK snow maps show 3 cities face flurries in Easter weekend forecast – full list

Weather forecasters say wet and windy conditions are on the cards for most across the extended Easter weekend - while modelling maps suggest some places could see snow

View 4 Images Snow (in purple) falling at around 3pm on Friday (Image: WXCharts)

Advanced weather forecasting maps show snow will fall in some parts of the UK over the extended Easter weekend.

‌



The ECMWF weather model suggests some flurries will hit the far north of Scotland on Friday afternoon - although more widespread snow is possible later in the weekend.

‌



The ECMWF maps for Sunday show snow falling in Belfast, Manchester and Glasgow at around midday, with sporadic wintry showers possible across northern England and Northern Ireland, while heavy snow falls over western parts of Scotland.

‌



The Met Office has told Brits to expect “unsettled” conditions across the Easter weekend, with an “increasing likelihood of wet and windy weather” for some areas.

View 4 Images More snow is possible on Sunday, the ECMWF model suggests (Image: WXCharts)

UK weather maps show England set for wall of snow as one county faces 17 inches READ MORE :

Met Office Deputy Chief Meteorologist, Steven Keates, said: “As we head into Good Friday and Easter Saturday, the weather is expected to turn more unsettled, with spells of rain at times, some of which could be heavy. This will be followed by sunny spells and showers, with the driest conditions likely towards the southeast of the UK.

‌



“It is also likely to become windy at times across all areas, particularly in exposed north-western locations. While there remains some uncertainty in the detail at this point in time, there is a strong signal for wet and windy conditions to continue into the Easter Weekend.”

View 4 Images Snow could fall on Friday and Sunday, maps suggest (Stock) (Image: PA)

BBC weather forecasters also say wet and windy conditions are likely. The BBC forecast states: “Stronger winds could develop during the Easter weekend, with gales possible across parts of Scotland and Northern Ireland as a vigorously deepening low pressure circulation approaches.

Article continues below

“There'll be some heavy rain, and it could also turn wet in Wales and the north and west of England as a frontal system edges across. Southern and eastern England may stay dry until late in the day or overnight.

View 4 Images Wet and windy conditions are likely for most this weekend (stock) (Image: PA)

“Sunday will be a chillier and showery day, with frequent and often wintry showers across northern and western Scotland. Sunny spells could be interrupted by sharp showers elsewhere. Southern and eastern England should see the fewest showers and the most sunshine.”

News.title: Urgent scam warning issued over online beach hut fraudsters
News.content:
Urgent scam warning issued over online beach hut fraudsters

Kent officials have warned people to stay vigilant after a series of beach hut listings posted on auction sites advertising exclusive properties turned out to be fraudulent

View 3 Images Officials have warned prospective buyers to take care following a series of fraudulent posts (Image: Getty Images)

eBay scammers have taken to the online auction platform and similar sites in a bid to sell people desperate to own a beachfront hut exclusive properties they don't even own.

‌



Would-be buyers have spoken out after encountering fraudsters with bogus listings advertising huts in Tankerton, near Whitstable, in Kent, on sites such as eBay for thousands of pounds below market value.

‌



Buyers lured in by the too-good-to-be-true prices have been left out in the cold, but only after the fraudsters went to incredible lengths to convince them to stump up the cash.

‌



In some cases, the criminals have broken into huts and invited property seekers for viewings while offering excuses for why they couldn't attend in person.

Nationwide customers with holiday booked urged to do two-second check READ MORE :

View 3 Images Beach hut associations have been told to 'spread the word to their members' about the scams (Image: Getty Images/iStockphoto)

Canterbury City Council (CCC) has said it is aware of multiple incidents of fraudulent selling, and has urged both buyers and owners to remain vigilant.

‌



The authority's cabinet member for economic development and inclusion and coastal towns, Councillor Chris Cornell, said people should be weary if they encounter an offer that "sounds too good to be true".

He said: "The golden rule is, if something sounds too good to be true, it generally is. As soon as we learned of people selling beach huts in Tankerton they do not own, we informed the beach hut owners and advised them to contact Kent Police and Report Fraud.

"We also notified the beach hut associations, so they could spread the word to their members. We would always advise beach hut owners to be vigilant for the potential for fraudulent activity such as this and to report any concerns they have to the police as swiftly as possible."

‌



Seaside beach huts are especially sought after in Kent, with several of the wooden structures in the picturesque suburb of Tankerton being sold for nearly £60,000 by genuine estate agents.

Others in Herne Bay and Whitstable are being sold for etween £27,000 and £52,000. Cllr Cornell added: "Our foreshore team is happy to provide advice on whether a hut sale is genuine if people contact us.

"While hut owners are permitted to sell privately and via whatever method they choose, our advice to prospective buyers is to only purchase huts through agents or the beach hut associations.

‌



"Sadly, the main victim in scams of this type will always be the unsuspecting purchaser." The warning has also been echoed by beach hut groups, with concerns buyers are already being caught out.

View 3 Images Beach huts in Kent can go for up to £60,000 (Image: CCC/Cover Images)

Sue Halfpenny, from the Herne Bay Beach Hut Association, said: "Canterbury City Council have made us aware of at least two incidents of fraud relating to beach huts sales. At the moment it appears that locally this is related to huts in Tankerton but we need to be watchful.

‌



"If you see anything relating to the sale of a beach hut that looks suspicious please send details to the Association with photos etc to hbbhoa@gmail.com.

"If you are looking to either buy or sell a beach hut we can help you - please contact using these online forms" The council says anyone concerned about a potential scam should report it to police or via the national fraud reporting service. Prospective buyers are also being urged to verify any sale before handing over money, with officials warning deals that appear significantly cheaper than usual should raise alarm bells.

An eBay spokesperson said: "Ensuring eBay is a safe and secure marketplace for our buyers and sellers is a top priority. eBay maintains a zero-tolerance policy against fraud and in the rare instance that one of our users is a victim of a scam, we advise them to report it immediately to their local police force, Action Fraud and eBay.

Article continues below

"We have dedicated teams that work closely with law enforcement, and they can investigate reported sellers and provide evidence to police as requested.”

News.title: Urgent warning to tourists as hotels become 'potential targets' for Iran strikes
News.content:
An urgent warning has been issued to tourists as hotels may be targeted by Iran or Iran-backed actors in the Middle East.

The US Department of State Consular Affairs today said it was "tracking reports of threats against locations where American citizens gather" in Saudi Arabia.

It added: "We advise US citizens that hotels and other gathering points including US businesses and US educational institutions may be potential targets."

The statement also reiterated a Worldwide Caution Security Alert issued by the department on March 22, which advised Americans worldwide to exercise increased caution.

It said the US Embassy in Riyadh has directed all US government employees to shelter in place, and urged all Americans in Saudi Arabia to do the same until further notice. It added: "To the extent possible, remain in your residence or another structure, and stay away from windows."

Image: The White House/AFP via Getty Im) The White House/AFP via Getty Im)

The department also shared advice for US citizens looking to get out of the Middle East. It said: "If you want to leave the Middle East, the US government is ready to assist by providing you the latest information about the departure options available.

"Saudi airspace remains open with frequent air traffic restrictions to address continued missile and drone threats. Riyadh, Jeddah, and Dammam airports remain open and operational, but travelers are advised to check their flight status directly with the airline due to possible delays and cancellations."

This comes as an American journalist has been kidnapped by an armed group in Baghdad. The Iraqi Interior Ministry confirmed a "foreign journalist was kidnapped by unknown individuals" in the Iraqi capital on Tuesday evening, adding that security forces are hunting down the perpetrators.

The journalist has been named as Shelly Kittleson, a US freelance reporter based in the Middle East and Afghanistan. Her work has appeared in Al-Monitor, Foreign Policy, the BBC World Service, New Lines Magazine, Politico and Al Majalla, according to her X profile.

The ministry said authorities intercepted a vehicle believed to belong to the kidnappers, which overturned as they attempted to flee, and that one suspect was arrested. Efforts to track down the remaining suspects and secure the release of the "abducted woman" are ongoing, it said.

Elizabeth Tsurkov, an Israeli-Russian graduate student from Princeton University, was kidnapped by an Iran-aligned Shia militia group during a research trip to Iraq in March 2023. She was freed in September 2025, with Iraqi Prime Minister Mohammed Shia al-Sudani saying at the time that her release was "a culmination of extensive efforts exerted by our security services over the course of many months".

News.title: Brit engineer found dead in Mumbai hotel while working on IPL cricket coverage
News.content:
Brit engineer found dead in Mumbai hotel while working on IPL cricket coverage

Jan William Langford, 76, was discovered unresponsive in his room at the five-star Trident Hotel in Mumbai's Nariman Point

View 3 Images Broadcast engineer Jan William Langford was found dead in Mumbai during the Indian Premier League T20 tournament

A British engineer working on Indian Premier League cricket coverage has been found dead in a Mumbai hotel room.

‌



Jan William Langford, 76, was discovered unresponsive in his room at the five-star Trident Hotel in Mumbai's Nariman Point. Mr Langford was working with the Board of Control for Cricket in India.

‌



The broadcast engineer reportedly returned to his room after the Mumbai Indians vs Kolkata Knight Riders clash at Wankhede Stadium on March 29.

‌



But when repeated calls to his room went unanswered the following day, alarmed hotel staff went to check on him. After getting no response, staff allegedly used a master key to enter, where they found him lying on the floor.

View 3 Images Jan William Langford's death in his room at the five-star Trident Hotel in Mumbai's Nariman Point is at the centre of an investigation (Image: Booking.com)

The hotel’s in-house doctor was called before the Brit was rushed to hospital and declared dead.

‌



The IPL Governing Council released a statement saying: “The IPL Governing Council and all stakeholders involved express their deepest condolences on the untimely demise of Mr Ian Williams Langford, a dedicated broadcast engineer, who was an integral part of our broadcast operations. Our thoughts and prayers are with his family and friends back home.

“The IPL is committed to providing all necessary support and assistance to Mr Langford’s family during this incredibly difficult time. The health, safety, and overall security of every member involved in the smooth functioning of the IPL continue to remain of utmost importance."

View 3 Images Mr Langford was working with the Board of Control for Cricket in India covering the IPL T20 tournament (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

‌



Nilesh Bagul, senior police officer at Marine Drive Police Station, said: “The hotel receptionist tried to contact him and called his room but there was no response. They waited and later decided to check on him. He was rushed to the city’s Bombay Hospital where doctors declared him dead.”

Mr Bagul confirmed that the British High Commission has been notified and Mr Langford’s son has been reached. A decision regarding the repatriation of the body will be made once the viscera report results are available.

Police have registered an accidental death report at Marine Drive Police Station, with investigations now underway. Officers added they have not found anything suspicious in his postmortem or any evidence of foul play. Officials have not yet confirmed the cause of death.

Article continues below

A spokesperson for the UK Foreign Office said: “We supported the family of a British national who has died in India and were in contact with the local authorities.”

News.title: Artemis 2 launch weather update as NASA lift-off could be postponed at any time
News.content:
Artemis 2 launch weather update as NASA lift-off could be postponed at any time

Weather conditions in Cape Canaveral will determine whether the Artemis 2 launch goes ahead on Wednesday, marking humanity's first Moon mission in decades

Artemis II - Nasa's mission to the moon

NASA has begun its countdown for humanity’s first launch to the Moon in more than 50 years - but the weather will determine whether the Artemis 2 crew actually takes off tomorrow.

‌



Four astronauts aboard the Space Launch System rocket could blast off from NASA's Kennedy Space Center in Cape Canaveral, Florida, on Wednesday evening. After a day in orbit around Earth, their Orion capsule will carry them to the Moon and back in the first crewed lunar mission since 1972. The nearly 10-day, 600,000-mile trip will end with the capsule safely splashing down in the Pacific Ocean.

‌



NASA has an extensive set of weather criteria that must be met for the Artemis 2 launch to go ahead. Conditions in Florida currently look favourable for Wednesday, with clear and dry weather forecast for much of the day. NASA said on Tuesday that, based on the current forecast, there is an "80 per cent" chance of a launch. If conditions fall outside acceptable limits, the space agency's meteorologists will "scrub" or cancel the mission. The main concerns are cloud coverage and the potential for high winds.

‌



View 3 Images The Artemis II crew (Image: Getty Images)

Meet the Artemis 2 crew set to launch in days on NASA's first Moon mission in 50 years READ MORE :

Artemis 2 launch may face new problem as scientists raise fears ahead of take off READ MORE :

Speaking at NASA's briefing on the mission on Monday, launch director Charlie Blackwell-Thompson said she felt "pretty good about our chances". Amit Kshatriya, NASA's associate administrator, said there were "no issues preventing us from pressing ahead", adding that the launch will only be delayed by the weather if conditions move out of an "acceptable range".

Weather forecast for NASA's Artemis 2 launch

Weather forecasting company AccuWeather appears to back NASA meteorologists' assessments. "The weather seems to be cooperating for a Wednesday launch," AccuWeather meteorologist Lydia Burroughs told Newsweek. "Showers from earlier in the day may be lingering in the area into the evening, but the risk for rain or lightning during the launch window is low."

‌



View 3 Images It will be humanity’s first launch to the Moon in more than 50 years (Image: AP)

Artemis 2 countdown begins as major update issued ahead of NASA moon mission READ MORE :

Artemis 2 manned Moon mission will be helped by Cornwall site playing key role READ MORE :

However, Burroughs told the outlet that sporadic thunderstorms are possible throughout the rest of the week into Monday, which could cause delays if a later launch become necessary. She added that winds are expected to remain light, with highs above 26C and lows between 15C and 20C.

NASA’s Artemis 2 mission was originally scheduled to launch in February but was delayed due to hydrogen fuel leaks. The leaks were fixed, but a helium pressurisation line later became clogged, forcing the rocket back to the hangar late last month.

Article continues below

View 3 Images Artemis 2 has been delayed for months (Image: NASA/ZUMA Press Wire Service/REX/Shutterstock)

Tim Peake says every astronaut on earth feels same about NASA Artemis II mission READ MORE :

The rocket returned to the pad one and a half weeks ago, and its crew arrived at the launch site on Friday after completing a 14-day quarantine. The crew includes commander Reid Wiseman, pilot Victor Glover, mission specialist Christina Koch - all NASA astronauts - and Canadian Space Agency astronaut Jeremy Hansen.

If the mission goes ahead this week and all goes smoothly, Koch will become the first woman to fly to the Moon, Glover will become the first black astronaut and first person of colour to travel into deep space, and Hansen will become the first Canadian and first non-American to reach Earth's only natural satellite. It marks a historic departure from the Apollo-era crews, who were exclusively white American men, many with military backgrounds.

News.title: Woman told to return £33k jackpot after William Hill claims technical glitch
News.content:
Woman told to return £33k jackpot after William Hill claims technical glitch

Gemma Bradley, 47, from Wakefield said she was 'crying with happiness' after seemingly winning the huge sum on the Jackpot Drop game before William Hill demanded it back

View 3 Images Gemma Bradley was 'crying with happiness' and planned to pay off her mortgage after thinking she had won big on William Hill's Jackpot Drop game last Monday (Image: SWNS)

A woman has been left 'absolutely gutted' after being told to return the £33,000 she apparently won in an online casino game.

‌



Gemma Bradley was among an unknown number of customers instructed to repay her jackpot after William Hill said their supposed wins on Monday, 16 March were caused by a technical fault.

‌



The bookmaker is understood to be in discussions with tens of thousands of customers following 'unintended jackpot behaviour' which resulted in 'incorrect payouts' being made during a 40-minute window that morning.

‌



Gemma, 47, said she was 'crying with happiness' and intended to clear her mortgage after believing she had struck it lucky on the Jackpot Drop game. The care assistant from Wakefield, Yorkshire, transferred £33,000 of the £47,182 winnings into her bank account.

Three year warning to anyone with NS&I Premium Bonds READ MORE :

Missing British EuroMillions winner with huge search for ticket in major town READ MORE :

View 3 Images Gemma has been ordered to pay back the £33K (Image: SWNS)

But her joy was fleeting after the firm contacted her the following day demanding the money back - alleging a technical problem had occurred, reports the Manchester Evening News.

‌



Gemma, who is now seeking assistance from gambling adjudicators, said: "I'm absolutely gutted. I haven't been sleeping properly. It's all I've been thinking about since Monday."

An Incident Report seemingly circulated by William Hill states there were 35,072 jackpot 'hits' during the malfunction compared to 518 over the equivalent period a week earlier.

Players turned to social media to reveal how their 'winnings' of up to £200,000 had been wiped out. Many claim they were still celebrating their fortunate victories when they found their online betting accounts had been frozen.

‌



Those impacted are believed to have received 'settlement agreements' proposing 11 per cent of the mistakenly awarded winnings if they return the money within three days - though many have chosen to challenge the matter.

View 3 Images Gemma had planned to pay off her mortgage with the money she thought she won (Image: Ann Bradley© SWNS)

Gemma and her 69-year-old mum Ann, who live together, were getting ready to leave the worry of mortgage payments behind them as they celebrated on Monday.

‌



Gemma, said: "We were crying with happiness. I'm 42 and I was under the impression that my mortgage was going to be paid off and my mum could enjoy her retirement a lot more."

She withdrew £33,000 - the maximum for a debit card - straight away and intended to take the remainder out the following day. But when she attempted to do precisely that, she couldn't access her William Hill account - and that evening a representative rang to explain the error and demand the £33,000 back.

"They said it was an issue at their end," she said, "so I'd have to pay it back and that I wouldn't be able to withdraw the rest of the funds. It's a good job I didn't book a holiday or something like that. What if it's happened to someone who's gone out and bought a car? I was quite sensible but it did get my hopes up."

‌



William Hill's terms and conditions state that they are entitled to withhold winnings or request their return in the event of technical errors. Gemma maintains the glitch was "not my fault" but says she is prepared to repay the money if required.

A William Hill spokesman said: "During a routine review of platform activity, we identified an issue affecting the Jackpot Drop game which resulted in incorrect sums being credited to players' balances and withdrawals being processed incorrectly.

"While we quickly identified and resolved this issue, for a short period of time funds were erroneously credited to some customer accounts that were not correctly generated through valid or properly functioning gameplay.

Article continues below

"We have contacted relevant customers to clarify the error, and - in certain cases - organise the return of the funds in line with our standard terms and conditions."
